subject: Re: Order schedule — anchored volume safeguard & packaging penalty redline
messages:
From: Sara Chen <sara.chen@novuscloud.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Order schedule redlines (volume safeguard + packaging penalty)

Hi Olga / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We reviewed the order schedule with legal and procurement and attached a redline (Novus_Cloud_Redline_v2.docx) that contains two main asks:

1) The "packaging penalty" language in the SOW that imposes a unilateral clawback for packaging SKU mismatch. We think the current draft is overly broad — it could trigger for expected SKU transitions during our pilot and early ramp. We propose removing the automatic penalty and replacing it with a 30-day remediation window plus a capped reconciliation.

2) The anchored-volume safeguard: the way the draft ties the floor/cap true-up to a single quarter could expose NovusCloud to a large retroactive charge. We propose a cap of 5% aggregate clawback across the first 12 months and an escrow mechanism for disputed amounts.

Attached is our marked draft with comments. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a 5% cap and the escrow approach? If not, please propose alternate thresholds — our goal is to protect predictable economics during the first-year product migration.

Sara
Sara Chen
Sr. Procurement Manager | NovusCloud
Attachment: Novus_Cloud_Redline_v2.docx (Word doc, redlines + comments)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Chen <sara.chen@novuscloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order schedule redlines (volume safeguard + packaging penalty)

Sara — thanks for the redline and clear asks. I reviewed the attached file briefly and looped in Karthik (sales lead) and Laura (pricing/legal ops) to weigh in. A few quick points and requests:

- We understand concerns around pilot SKUs triggering a packaging penalty. Redwood is open to removing an automatic penalty for pilot/transition SKUs, but we need a clear definition of "pilot" and objective gating criteria so this doesn't become open-ended. Can you propose how Novus will designate pilot SKUs?

- On the anchored-volume true-up: a 5% aggregate clawback cap across 12 months is a reasonable starting position to discuss, but we typically prefer a staggered clawback schedule (tiered % by under-delivery bucket) rather than a single aggregate cap. That said, the escrow idea is workable.

- To keep things moving, we'll produce a tracked-changes draft that replaces the packaging penalty with a limited remediation and introduces a tiered clawback with an optional escrow hold for disputed sums. Laura — can you produce the markup by tomorrow EOD?

Next steps: Laura will send an internal redline, Karthik and I will propose negotiation points and a suggested cap schedule for Novus to review. Sara — if you can reply with the pilot-SKU definition and current expected SKU churn in months 0-6, that will help us calibrate the thresholds.

Best,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Sara Chen <sara.chen@novuscloud.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order schedule redlines (volume safeguard + packaging penalty)

Thanks Olga — quick answers below and a small clarification in-line.

- Pilot SKU designation: Novus will label up to 8 SKUs as "pilot" in writing at contract signing and may add up to 4 additional SKUs during the first 90 days with mutual written agreement (email ok). Pilot SKUs are exempt from packaging-penalty reconciliation for months 0-3.

- Expected churn: we expect ~12-15% SKU churn month-to-month in months 0-3 and 6-8% thereafter as product listings stabilize.

- On the clawback cap: Novus' preference is a firm 5% cap on aggregate clawback for months 0-12 (calculated as 5% of committed annual spend). The escrow would be third-party custody of amounts in dispute pending reconciliation no longer than 90 days.

We appreciate Redwood doing a tracked draft. If you can include an explicit formula for how the aggregate cap is calculated (annual committed spend * 5%) and where escrow funds would be held, that will help procurement sign off.

Sara

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Chen <sara.chen@novuscloud.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order schedule redlines (volume safeguard + packaging penalty)

Sara — appreciate the clarity and the pilot SKU mechanism. A few commercial counterpoints from Redwood:

1) Cap mechanics: instead of a single hard 5% cap, we propose a blended approach that shields both parties while keeping incentives aligned:
   - Months 0-3: no clawback for pilot SKUs (per your proposal).
   - Months 0-6: under-delivery clawback at 2% of deficit for the first 7.5% of shortfall, then 6% for the next band up to 15% shortfall (cumulative).
   - Months 7-12: reduced rates (1% then 3%) to allow stabilization.
   - We will cap total aggregate clawback at 6% of committed annual spend, but we can agree to a hard operational escrow up to 5% while disputes are resolved. This gives Novus the operational certainty of a 5% escrow hold while allowing Redwood to preserve a modest governance cap in extreme cases.

2) Packaging penalty: Redwood is comfortable removing the automatic penalty for pilot SKUs and replacing it with a 30-day remediation plan and a one-time reconciliation fee limited to replacement-cost differential (not full ARR), with an explicit maximum per-SKU reconciliation amount (we'll propose $X per SKU in the draft).

3) Documentation: we'll produce a clean tracked version that implements the banded clawback + escrow language and an appendix with the formula examples. Laura — can you confirm language and whether procurement prefers escrow administered via a neutral custodian or via HubSpot escrow account?

If Novus prefers a single 5% cap as a contractual maximum, we can discuss bridging language that writes the 5% escrow as the operational maximum with a Redwood-side governance carveout for fraud/intentional misreporting.

Karthik
Head of Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Novus redline — next steps and owner mapping

Team — summarizing action items from the Novus exchange so we have a clear handoff for legal and CSM: 

- Laura: produce tracked-changes draft implementing the banded clawback (Karthik's bands) + optional 5% escrow language; include a worked example table and an explicit formula (committed annual spend * percent). Due: Mon 22 Mar EOD. Attachment name to use: RW-OrderSchedule-proposed-redline.docx.

- Karthik: confirm the per-SKU maximum reconciliation figure ($X placeholder) and prefer neutral third-party custodian for escrow. Please propose final dollar cap by Monday.

- Olga: I'll send Novus the banded illustration and confirm pilot SKU registration process (email confirmation acceptable).

We should aim to converge on commercial language before involving legal redline round 3. Thanks — moving quickly here will help close before their quarter-end.

Olga
